output.subject: We've received your complaint about your rewards points
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us about your rewards points. We have received your complaint and want to make sure we've understood it.

You told us that a change to the rewards program means your points are now worth about half as much when used for travel. You mentioned that you had saved 48,000 points, which you understood to be worth $480 in travel credit, and that they now come to $240. You explained that you had been saving them for flights to visit your grandchildren, and you told us you feel strongly that this is unfair, describing it as basically fraud. You also mentioned that the change may have been announced in an email you didn't read.

We can hear how disappointing this is, especially given what you were saving those points for, and we're sorry for the frustration it has caused.

Your complaint is now with a specialist team, who will review the points you've raised and respond to you within 10 business days.

Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Confirm whether and when the rewards program change took effect, and the before/after travel redemption values for this customer's 48,000 points.
Customer describes the change as 'basically fraud'; decide how the specialist team's response should address that allegation.

Customer acknowledges notice may have been sent by email they didn't read; intake lists 'inadequate notice' as an issue, but the customer did not claim notice was missing. Check what notice was sent and when.
Request to restore the previous value is implied, not explicit; decide whether any remedy or goodwill gesture is appropriate.
Customer's phone number appeared in the complaint and was left out of the draft; confirm preferred contact method.
